walkthroughs.body_html:
A triad is built by stacking two 3rds. Pick a root, skip one letter for the 3rd, skip again for the 5th. C major triad = C-E-G. F major triad = F-A-C.

If the 3rd is a major 3rd (4 semitones), the triad is major. If it's a minor 3rd (3 semitones), the triad is minor.

In any major key, the three most important chords are I (tonic), IV (subdominant) and V (dominant). In C major: C, F and G.

You can harmonise almost any melody using just these three chords — the basis of folk songs, hymns and countless pop hits.

Same root, different 3rd — that's the trick. C major (C-E-G) sounds bright; C minor (C-E♭-G) sounds darker. Only one note changes!

In a major key, chords I, IV and V are major. In a minor key, chord i is minor, iv is minor and V is often kept major (using a raised 7th to make the dominant cadence stronger).
